message.reasoning:
The user is playing Monopoly as p2 (grok-4.7).

Pacific Avenue is up for auction. The current bid is $102. I have $653 cash and own Pennsylvania Avenue. Pacific would complete two of three greens. p4 has $1703 and is in jail. They are willing to contest. I will drop out. I will not overpay.

I am reconsidering the drop. Pacific is cheap at auction and would block p4 from completing the green set. I still need North Carolina Avenue.

I am calculating the roll from Pennsylvania Railroad. I need to check what space I land on.

Rolling from Pennsylvania Railroad lands on Community Chest or Tennessee Avenue. I am checking the rent for Tennessee with three houses.

Standard orange rent is $200 with two houses. I am checking the probability of rolling a 1 from Pennsylvania Railroad.

Rolling 3 or 4 from Pennsylvania Railroad lands on Tennessee or New York. Both cost $550 or $600. I would be short by $103 or $53. A $150 bid leaves only $503. That is too little to cover New York without mortgaging. The total mortgage capacity is only $300.

A $180 bid leaves $473. That covers a New York rent of $600 after mortgaging. Mortgaging greens and browns is risky for building. Pacific blocks the opponent from completing the green set. Only North Carolina Avenue remains unowned.

Pacific alone is worth little. Undeveloped rent is only $26. Building the green set would cost hundreds in houses. I will raise to about $180–$200 and then drop out.

A slow $103 bid would start a bidding war. I should jump higher to test p4's resolve.

I am reconsidering my ceiling. Pacific is cheap at auction, but North Carolina Avenue and the red set are more valuable than greens. I need cash for those properties too.

A $200 bid leaves only $453. That is too little to buy North Carolina Avenue. The red set is the higher priority. Pacific is a side quest. I cannot buy reds now. I must decide whether spending cash on Pacific prevents buying reds later.

p1 already ended their turn after landing on Pacific. I will roll from Pennsylvania Railroad next. I can land on reds and B&O this turn, but not greens, because those spaces require rolls of 16 or 17.

I can afford to bid up to about $400 and still buy Illinois, Kentucky, Indiana, or B&O. The real constraint is the orange rent risk and the need for cash to buy North Carolina later. I will raise the bid higher.

I am weighing a $150, $180, or $201 bid. p4 is a grinder who raised from $35 to $102. They likely have a ceiling. Forcing them to spend $200 on a single green they cannot complete is a minor cost for them given their $1703 cash. I will raise substantially to either win or make them pay.

I am weighing whether p4 will pay under $300 to block me. They already own three railroads and the electric company. They also hold two of three light blue properties. They want a yellow monopoly, but I am the Ventnor blocker. If they refuse to spend that much, I should drop out and save cash for reds.

I am now weighing a concrete trade-off. I could drop out and keep my full $653 cash for reds and orange survival. Or I could bid $150–$180 to win Pacific as a blocker. I need to judge whether that blocker is worth more than $100.

Completing the green set is now nearly impossible without Pacific. The red set remains the best winning path. Building browns is too slow and weak.

I will bid $160 or $175 to jump past p4's matching. A large raise may make them drop out and I can win Pacific cheap. I am checking if $175 is a fair price for that blocker.

I will bid $150. That is a modest raise above the $103 minimum and enough to test p4's commitment.

I am weighing a strategic public message to make p4 overbid. I will either sound committed or confident. Pacific gives two of three greens and blocks the opponent. It ties up cash and is expensive to develop. North Carolina Avenue remains unowned and still contestable.

I will bid $151. This leaves room to raise again if p4 matches. I am checking p4's history to judge their bidding style.

p4 is a quiet grinder with $1703. They will likely keep bidding to deny me the Pacific blocker, perhaps up to $200–$300. I will not match that. My cash is too valuable for reds.
